Controlled calibration now gives direct evidence for preserving genuine first-level variance information. Under an ideal Gaussian hierarchy with independent vhat = v * chi-square(df) / df, native PM/mKH reaches 8.85% null rejection at n=80, reversed variances, tau squared zero, first-level df=8, versus 4.16% with known variances. The provider agrees with independent metafor calculations. First-level df is not the group residual df; uncertainty origin, serial-noise estimation and run combination cannot be inferred from an SE array alone.

Report: docs/verification/group-controls-2026-09-08.md. The next research ticket bd-01M21BNZR9ZBRAYY9JD5WCQ8KX evaluates joint effect-and-variance Gaussian bootstrap. Synthetic experiments can proceed independently, but real application admission needs the provenance contract owned here. No df cutoff or approximation is silently admitted by the current study.
